title: DPCexplorer Docker, Kubernetes, and GitHub CI/CD Deployment Plan
status: Milestones 0-2 completed; Kubernetes and CI/CD milestones planned

self_sufficiency_contract.definition: A checkpoint is complete only when the complete application passes the common smoke tests in an explicitly named working environment.
self_sufficiency_contract.before_kubernetes_cutover: The verified local Docker deployment remains the working full application while new Kubernetes resources are built in parallel.
self_sufficiency_contract.after_kubernetes_cutover: The currently deployed Kubernetes release remains available until the replacement release passes readiness and the common smoke tests.
self_sufficiency_contract.substep_rule: Creating storage, loading data, restoring PostgreSQL, running migrations, and starting pods are substeps. None is considered a completed checkpoint on its own.
self_sufficiency_contract.failure_rule: If any substep fails, do not mark the checkpoint complete. Keep or restore the last environment that passed the full smoke test.
required_checkpoint_evidence: Known protein, Pfam, DPCfam, and DPCstruct queries work.
The admin interface works in its intended read-only mode.
The rollback target remains identified and usable.

kubernetes_profile.existing_dpcdom_resources: Training resources only. Keep them until the parallel DPCexplorer stack passes the full Kubernetes smoke test, then remove them.

permanent_web_recommended.description: Two identical Django/Gunicorn containers in separate Kubernetes pods.

permanent_web_initial.description: One Django/Gunicorn container during the first internal Kubernetes validation.

permanent_postgresql_preproduction.description: One CloudNativePG PostgreSQL instance in kdevel. PostgreSQL is not embedded in the Django container.

total_permanent_preproduction_after_scal.description: Two web containers plus one CloudNativePG PostgreSQL container.

temporary_per_release.description: A migration container runs as a Kubernetes Job and exits when migrations finish.

temporary_first_installation.description: A data-loader container populates the shared biological-data volume and then exits.

common_smoke_tests: A known protein ID search works.
A known Pfam ID search works.
A known DPCfam metacluster page works.
DPCfam FASTA, MSA, and HMM files are downloadable.
A known DPCstruct metacluster page works.
The 3D structure viewer loads a PDB file.
The large archive download links work.
Scientific tables remain read-only unless explicitly configured otherwise.
The liveness endpoint reports that Django is running.
The readiness endpoint confirms that PostgreSQL and biological-data storage are available.

milestones.name: Establish a working baseline
milestones.goal: Prove that the current application, database, and biological files work before changing deployment technology.
tasks: Run the current application normally.
Confirm that PostgreSQL contains the DPC scientific tables and Django auth, admin, and session tables.
Select one known protein ID, Pfam ID, DPCfam metacluster ID, and DPCstruct metacluster ID for repeatable testing.
Record the common smoke-test results.
completion_check: Run every common smoke test against the existing non-containerized application.
milestones.end_state: The existing application continues to work exactly as before.
milestones.rollback: No rollback is needed because this milestone does not change the application.

milestones.name: Make Django production-ready without Docker
milestones.goal: Prepare Django for production while it still runs directly from the Python virtual environment.
tasks: Add Gunicorn to requirements.txt.
Run the WSGI application with Gunicorn on port 8000.
Add /health/live for process health.
Add /health/ready to check PostgreSQL and a biological-data sentinel file.
Change logging from a local file to stdout.
Set DEBUG=False and configure ALLOWED_HOSTS.
Configure CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS for the production HTTPS URL.
Configure SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER for the Kubernetes Ingress.
Replace STATICFILES_STORAGE with Django's current STORAGES configuration.
Separate normal static assets from biological data by introducing DPC_DATA_ROOT and DPC_DATA_URL.
Run python manage.py check --deploy.
completion_check: Start the application with Gunicorn from the virtual environment.
Run every common smoke test.
Confirm that logs appear on stdout.
Confirm that readiness fails when PostgreSQL is unavailable.
Confirm that readiness fails when the biological-data directory is unavailable.
milestones.end_state: The complete application works in production mode without Docker.
milestones.rollback: Run the previous application revision using the original virtual-environment startup method.

milestones.name: Dockerize the application
milestones.goal: Run the complete application as one Docker container while using an external PostgreSQL database and mounted biological data.
tasks: Create a Dockerfile based on python:3.12-slim.
Install dependencies from requirements.txt.
Copy only application code and normal static assets.
Run collectstatic during the image build.
Create and use a non-root runtime user.
Start Gunicorn on 0.0.0.0:8000.
Create a .dockerignore file.
Exclude .venv, .git, logs, dataframes, downloads, production_files, notebooks, and profiling reports from the image.
Pass Django and PostgreSQL configuration through environment variables.
Mount the biological-data directory read-only at /data.
Do not include PostgreSQL in the application container.
Do not run setup_dpcexplorer_data.sh during every image build or container startup.
completion_check: Start one Docker container against the existing populated PostgreSQL database.
Run every common smoke test.
Restart the container and confirm that no application data is lost.
Confirm that stopping the container does not affect PostgreSQL.
Confirm that the image does not contain the approximately 40 GB generated data directory.
milestones.end_state: The complete application works from one portable Docker image.
milestones.rollback: Stop the container and start the working non-containerized Gunicorn deployment from milestone 1.

milestones.name: Build a complete kdevel preproduction deployment in parallel
milestones.goal: Deploy and verify the complete application in the dpcdom namespace on kdevel without sacrificing the last working full application.
milestones.checkpoint_policy: The infrastructure operations inside a checkpoint are substeps. A checkpoint closes only after the named working environment passes every common smoke test.

checkpoints.name: Create reviewable Kubernetes manifests
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete local Docker application from milestone 2.
substeps: Create k8s/base plus k8s/overlays/kdevel and k8s/overlays/kprod.

Define the dpcexplorer-web Deployment and Service, dpcexplorer-data RWX PersistentVolumeClaim, dpcexplorer-postgresql CloudNativePG cluster, ConfigMap references, Secret references, migration Job, data-loader Job, and Ingress.
Reference an immutable GHCR image tag or digest.
Keep all real passwords, Django secret keys, certificates, and kubeconfig data out of Git.
Render and inspect the kdevel manifests with kubectl kustomize without changing the cluster.
completion_check: The kdevel manifests render successfully.
The rendered resource names, namespace, storage classes, access modes, ports, probes, and secret references are correct.
Run the complete local Docker smoke-test script and confirm every common smoke test still passes.
checkpoints.end_state: A reviewable Kubernetes design exists, and the complete application is still working locally.
checkpoints.rollback: Discard or correct only the uncommitted manifest changes; the local Docker application remains unchanged.

checkpoints.name: Deploy one complete internal Kubernetes stack
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application on kdevel through a local port-forward; the local Docker deployment remains a fallback.
substeps: Publish the verified application image to GHCR using the Git commit SHA and configure image pulling in dpcdom if the package is private.
Create the 70Gi dpcexplorer-data RWX PersistentVolumeClaim using cephfs-hdd-ec.
Create the one-instance dpcexplorer-postgresql CloudNativePG cluster with 50Gi on rbd-nvme-replica.
Load the biological data with an idempotent Job and create the readiness sentinel only after validation succeeds.
Create a verified pg_dump from the working database and restore it into database dpcexplorer through dpcexplorer-postgresql-rw.
Run Django migrations as a one-time Job. Remember that migrations do not create the scientific tables whose models use managed=False.
Create new DPCexplorer ConfigMaps and Secrets; do not reuse the fake OpenProject secret.
Deploy one dpcexplorer-web pod, its ClusterIP Service, and the liveness and readiness probes.
Use kubectl port-forward for internal validation.
Keep the existing training resources and the local Docker application until all completion checks pass.
completion_check: The PostgreSQL cluster, data-loader Job, database restore, and migration Job have completed successfully.
The web pod is Ready and both health endpoints pass.
Run every common smoke test through the port-forward, including the 3D viewer and real downloads.
Confirm the exact application image SHA or digest.
Confirm the local Docker rollback environment is still usable.
checkpoints.end_state: The complete application works internally on kdevel with PostgreSQL and biological data, without depending on an Ingress.
checkpoints.rollback: Delete or repair only the new dpcexplorer-* resources and continue using the verified local Docker deployment.

checkpoints.name: Expose and verify the complete kdevel application over HTTPS
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application on kdevel through its preproduction HTTPS address.
substeps: Confirm a dedicated preproduction hostname with the Kubernetes administrator.
Create DNS and TLS configuration and an Ingress using the approved kdevel ingress class, expected to be nginx-devel.
Configure ALLOWED_HOSTS, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, proxy HTTPS handling, secure cookies, and production error pages for the preproduction hostname.
Route the Ingress to the dpcexplorer-web Service.
completion_check: The TLS certificate is valid and HTTP redirects to HTTPS.
Both health endpoints pass through the HTTPS address.
Run every common smoke test through HTTPS, including the 3D viewer, admin login, and large downloads.
Confirm that the internal Kubernetes route and local Docker rollback environment remain available.
checkpoints.end_state: The complete application works over HTTPS on kdevel.
checkpoints.rollback: Remove or correct only the new Ingress and continue using the internal port-forward or local Docker deployment.

checkpoints.name: Validate high availability and remove training resources
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete HTTPS application on kdevel with two web replicas and one PostgreSQL instance.
substeps: Scale dpcexplorer-web from one replica to two.
Confirm that both replicas mount the same RWX biological-data volume read-only.
Delete one web pod and confirm that Kubernetes replaces it without losing service.
Test deployment rollback using a previously verified immutable image.
After all tests pass, remove only the disposable training dpcdom-django and dpcdom-postgresql resources approved for replacement.
Confirm that namespace CPU, memory, PVC, and storage usage remain within quota.
completion_check: Two web replicas are Ready and the PostgreSQL instance is Ready.
The application remains available while one web pod is replaced.
A rollback to a known-good image works.
Run every common smoke test again through HTTPS after cleanup.
Record the running image digest and the database backup or restore point.
checkpoints.end_state: kdevel contains the complete, resilient preproduction DPCexplorer stack, with three permanent containers: two web and one PostgreSQL.
checkpoints.rollback: Redeploy the recorded known-good image, scale back to one web replica if necessary, and restore PostgreSQL from the recorded backup or restore point. Do not remove the local fallback until this checkpoint is accepted.

milestones.name: Add GitHub CI/CD while keeping kdevel working
milestones.goal: Make GitHub test, publish, and deploy immutable images without allowing a failed automation change to replace the working kdevel release.

checkpoints.name: Add non-deploying pull-request CI
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The existing complete HTTPS application on kdevel.
substeps: Create a GitHub Actions pull-request workflow with a small temporary PostgreSQL service and test fixtures.
Install dependencies and run Django system checks, tests, and migration consistency checks.
Build the Docker image, start it, test liveness, and scan it for important vulnerabilities.
Protect the main branch and require the workflow to pass.
Do not grant this workflow Kubernetes deployment permission.
completion_check: An intentional test failure blocks a test pull request.
After fixing the failure, all CI gates pass.
The workflow has not changed the kdevel cluster.
Run every common smoke test against the currently deployed kdevel application.
checkpoints.end_state: Pull requests are gated by CI, and the complete kdevel application remains working.
checkpoints.rollback: Disable or revert the workflow change; keep the currently deployed kdevel release.

checkpoints.name: Publish one immutable GHCR image after merge
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The existing complete HTTPS application on kdevel, plus a verified deployable image in GHCR.
substeps: Extend the main-branch workflow to build the image once after CI passes.
Push the image to GHCR with the exact Git commit SHA and record its digest.
Configure package visibility and image-pull authentication with least privilege.
Do not deploy the new package automatically in this checkpoint.
completion_check: The GHCR package exists with the expected commit-SHA tag.
The recorded digest identifies the exact tested image.
A clean pull and container liveness check succeed.
Run every common smoke test against the unchanged kdevel deployment.
checkpoints.end_state: GitHub produces a verified immutable image while the complete kdevel application continues serving.
checkpoints.rollback: Stop publishing new images and continue using the currently deployed known-good digest.

checkpoints.name: Add protected automated deployment to kdevel
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete HTTPS application on kdevel, deployed from GitHub using a verified immutable digest.
substeps: Create a protected GitHub kdevel Environment and store only the required deployment credentials there.
Use a restricted Kubernetes identity for the dpcdom namespace and a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner if the Kubernetes API is private.
Deploy the exact digest already produced by CI without rebuilding it.
Run the migration Job first and stop the release if it fails.
Perform a rolling web Deployment update, wait for readiness, and run automated HTTPS smoke tests.
Keep old Ready pods serving until the new pods pass readiness.
If post-deployment tests fail, roll back the web Deployment to the recorded previous digest; never automatically reverse database migrations.
completion_check: Deploy a harmless visible change through the protected workflow.
Confirm the expected commit SHA and digest are running in two Ready web pods.
Run every common smoke test through the kdevel HTTPS address.
Deploy the previous known-good digest and then restore the new digest, running the full smoke suite after each deployment.
checkpoints.end_state: Approved kdevel releases are tested, published, migrated, deployed, verified, and reversible while the complete application remains available.
checkpoints.rollback: Redeploy the recorded previous immutable digest and keep database migrations forward-compatible.

milestones.name: Promote the complete application to kprod in parallel
milestones.goal: Build and validate a separate production stack, then move the public URL only after the complete application works on kprod.

checkpoints.name: Build a complete internal kprod stack
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application on kprod through an internal validation route; kdevel remains the external fallback.
substeps: Confirm the kprod namespace, quotas, storage classes, ingress class, network policy, and backup policy with the administrator.
Apply the kprod overlay to create production RWX biological-data storage and a production CloudNativePG cluster with the agreed high-availability and backup settings.
Populate and validate the data volume, restore a verified database backup, and run migrations.
Deploy the same immutable image digest already accepted on kdevel, plus its Service and health probes.
Keep the complete kdevel application running throughout the build.
completion_check: All kprod database, storage, migration, web, Service, and probe checks pass.
Run every common smoke test through a port-forward or private validation route.
Confirm the kprod database backup and restore procedure.
Confirm the complete kdevel environment remains available as the rollback target.
checkpoints.end_state: The complete application works internally on kprod before any public DNS cutover.
checkpoints.rollback: Remove or repair only the new kprod resources and continue serving the complete application from kdevel.

checkpoints.name: Validate kprod over HTTPS before public cutover
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application on kprod over a temporary or controlled HTTPS validation address; kdevel remains live.
substeps: Create a temporary production-validation hostname or use a controlled host mapping approved by the administrator.
Configure the production Ingress and TLS certificate without moving the public dpcexplorer DNS record.
Validate production security settings, downloads, viewer behavior, pod replacement, and database connectivity.
completion_check: TLS and HTTPS routing to kprod pass.
Run every common smoke test against kprod over HTTPS.
Replace one web pod and confirm the complete app remains available.
Confirm kdevel still passes the common smoke tests.
checkpoints.end_state: The complete kprod application is proven over HTTPS before receiving public traffic.
checkpoints.rollback: Remove or correct the validation Ingress and continue serving from kdevel.

checkpoints.name: Cut over the public production URL
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application at https://dpcexplorer.areasciencepark.it/ on kprod; kdevel is retained as a rollback environment.
substeps: Lower DNS TTL in advance if the administrator permits it and record the previous DNS target.
Point dpcexplorer.areasciencepark.it to the approved kprod Ingress.
Monitor rollout, application logs, health endpoints, error rates, PostgreSQL, storage, and certificate status.
Keep kdevel intact until the production acceptance period ends.
completion_check: The public URL presents the correct valid certificate and routes to kprod.
Run every common smoke test against the public URL.
Confirm the expected immutable image digest is running with the intended number of Ready replicas.
Confirm the recorded DNS and image rollback procedures are usable.
checkpoints.end_state: The complete application is serving users from kprod at the final public URL.
checkpoints.rollback: Restore the previous DNS target or route, then redeploy the last known-good image digest if required.

checkpoints.name: Automate protected kprod promotion
checkpoints.working_environment_at_end: The complete application at the public kprod URL, deployed by a protected GitHub promotion workflow.
substeps: Create a protected GitHub production Environment with mandatory human approval.
Promote the exact image digest that already passed kdevel; never rebuild it for production.
Run forward-compatible migrations, rolling deployment, readiness checks, and the automated public smoke suite.
Retain the previous known-good digest and kdevel environment for rollback.
completion_check: Promote a harmless accepted kdevel release to kprod with manual approval.
Confirm the exact same digest is running in kdevel and kprod.
Run every common smoke test against the public URL.
Exercise a controlled rollback to a known-good digest and restore the intended release, verifying the full app after both operations.
checkpoints.end_state: A release can move safely from GitHub to kdevel and then to kprod, with the complete application verified at every checkpoint.
checkpoints.rollback: Redeploy the previous immutable digest, preserve forward-compatible database state, and use the recorded traffic or DNS rollback if application availability requires it.

final_release_flow: Run required CI checks and preserve the currently working deployment.
After merge, build the application image once and push it to GHCR using the Git commit SHA and an immutable digest.
Deploy that digest to kdevel, run forward-compatible migrations, wait for the rolling update, and run every common smoke test.
Keep or roll back the kdevel release based on the results.
After kdevel acceptance, request protected production approval.
Promote the exact same digest to kprod without rebuilding it.
Run forward-compatible migrations, wait for the rolling update, and run every common smoke test against the public URL.
Keep or roll back the kprod release while retaining the last verified environment and digest.
